# Hermes Agent: Onboarding & Troubleshooting FAQ

### 1. General & Platform Setup

**Is there a Web UI/Dashboard?**
Yes. Run `hermes dashboard` to launch the local web server at `http://127.0.0.1:9119`. It includes a full browser-based Chat tab embedding the Hermes TUI.

**What platforms and architectures are supported?**
- **Windows**: Native Windows 10/11 is a Tier 1 platform supported via the official `install.ps1` PowerShell script. *(Note: The Web Dashboard embedded terminal pane requires a POSIX PTY, so WSL2 is recommended if using that specific pane).*
- **Docker / NAS (UGOS, Synology, unRAID)**: Official images support multi-arch (`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` for Apple Silicon / Raspberry Pi). For NAS volume permission issues (`[Errno 13] Permission denied`), set `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) environment variables.
- **Android / Termux**: Supported via curated dependencies (`termux-all`) and dynamic `TMPDIR` paths.

**How do I report a security vulnerability?**
Do not open public GitHub issues. Submit reports via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) or email `security@nousresearch.com` per `SECURITY.md`.

---

### 2. LLMs & Provider Configuration

**Why is my local model (e.g., Qwen 4B/9B) slow or timing out?**
Hermes injects full tool definitions (~45 schemas) into each call. Small local models struggle under high context token loads. To optimize:
- Run `hermes tools` and disable unneeded toolsets.
- Use `terminal.backend: local` to remove container overhead.
- Use 32B+ parameter models for tool-heavy autonomous tasks.

**Why does Hermes ignore my local `base_url` and fail with 401 errors?**
When `provider: auto` is set, Hermes scans the environment for API keys (e.g., `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). If found, it routes to that cloud provider instead of local endpoints. Set `provider: custom` explicitly in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.

**How do I configure specific providers?**
- **Ollama Cloud**: Supported natively via the `ollama-cloud` provider with base endpoint `https://ollama.com/v1`.
- **Azure AI Foundry**: Run `hermes setup` (auto-detects `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`) or set `provider: azure-foundry`.
- **Google Gemini**: Legacy CLI OAuth is removed. Configure standard API keys via `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY`.
- **Claude Pro/Max vs. API**: Claude API keys always bill as pay-per-token API usage. Subscription allowance usage requires OAuth authentication.
- **Vision on Custom Endpoints**: Add `supports_vision: true` under your model configuration to pass native image payloads.
- **Local Token Usage Tracking**: Hermes automatically passes `stream_options: {include_usage: true}` for OpenAI-compatible streaming endpoints (e.g., LocalAI).

**Is automatic cost-based model routing (`smart_model_routing`) supported?**
No. Complexity-based dynamic model switching has been intentionally removed. Use manual model switches (`/model` or `hermes chat -m <model>`), or configure subagent tiers via `delegation.provider` / `delegation.model`.

---

### 3. Messaging Gateways (Telegram, Discord, Matrix, etc.)

**How do I configure messaging gateways?**
Run the interactive wizard: `hermes gateway setup`. It prompts for tokens, allowed users, and channel bindings without manual `.env` editing.

**Why am I getting "Unauthorized user" errors on Telegram?**
`allowed_chats` is only a group-chat whitelist, not a user authorization key. To authorize users:
1. Set `allow_from: "<USER_ID>"` under `telegram:` in `config.yaml` (`TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS`).
2. Or use DM pairing: DM the bot, obtain the pairing code, and run `hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`.
3. Or set `allow_all: true` to permit all users.

**Can gateways send/receive files and media?**
- **Inbound**: Authorized users can upload text files and code (`.py`, `.txt`), which are injected directly into context.
- **Outbound**: Local files and generated documents are dispatched via native platform handlers (Matrix `m.file`, email SMTP attachments, Telegram images, and DingTalk Markdown media). MCP base64 images (`MEDIA:<path>`) are also forwarded automatically.

**Can I run multiple bots/accounts or per-channel personas?**
- **Multi-Profile**: Hermes supports gateway multiplexing where one gateway process manages multiple isolated profiles (separate sessions, memory, credentials).
- **Per-Channel Personas**: Use the `channel_prompts` configuration map in Discord, Telegram, Slack, or Mattermost configs to assign custom system prompts per channel ID.
- **Session Restarts**: Interrupted chats are preserved as `resume_pending`. Use `/resume` to restore conversation history.

---

### 4. Agent Execution, Memory & Extensibility

**Why did my agent stop due to a tool-call limit?**
Hermes enforces a per-session limit (`agent.max_turns`, default 90; overridable via `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`). For long-running autonomous workflows, use `/goal <task>` (Ralph loop), which persists across turns and supports `/goal resume`.

**How does memory work (`SOUL.md` vs. `USER.md` vs. `MEMORY.md`)?**
- `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`: Defines agent personality and system identity.
- `~/.hermes/USER.md`: Stores persistent facts about the user (`target="user"`).
- `MEMORY.md`: General working memory.
- *Third-party memory engines (e.g., Honcho, local memory)*: In-tree memory additions are closed. Install standalone plugins to `~/.hermes/plugins/`. Local Honcho connections (`localhost`) require no remote API key.

**How do I add custom tools and plugins?**
Build custom tools as standalone plugins in `~/.hermes/plugins/` and enable them using `hermes plugins enable <plugin_name>`.

**Observability & Telemetry:**
- **Execution Tracking**: Opt-in to Langfuse tracing with `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`.
- **Skill Usage Metrics**: View tool and skill usage stats via `hermes insights` or the `/insights` chat command.
